newsitem.title: USA: Morgan Stanley sees value in Philippines debt swap.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Stanley sees value in Philippines debt swap.

text.p: The Philippine Brady bond swap highlights the attractiveness of its Eurobonds of shorter maturity, Morgan Stanley said in a research report.

"A successful global should highlight the flatness of the Philippine Erobond curve," said emerging markets fixed income analyst Khalid Azim. "A 20-year Philippine global at a minimum spread of 225 basis points makes shorter maturity Philppine Eurobonds look attractive."
For example, the Philippine Samurai 5 of 2003 is at LIBOR plus 150 bp, or about 175 bp over treasuries. Or PLDT's 9-7/8 bond maturing 2005, at about 228 bp, looks cheap by comparison, he noted.
The success of the global/par exchange could boost the the intermediate portion of the Philippine yield curve by as much as 50 bps," Azim said.

The Philippines offered to exchange new fixed and floating rate global bonds of up to $1.9 billion Philippine Par bonds. Holders of pars can submit a bid for the new global offering at spread of 225 bp, or better, over U.S. Treasury for the fixed global, or a minimum of 175 bp over LIBOR for the 15-year floating globals.
Morgan Stanley estimates that half of Philippine Par bonds are held in domestic institutions, which would be inclined to exchange for higher yielding uncollateralized paper.
